osmTags.inscription: 1768-1774 In this house, lived Thomas Paine, writer and revolutionary
Thomas Paine, 1737‒1809, here expounded his revolutionary politics. This inn is regarded as a cradle of American Independence which helped to found with pen and sword.

Eve Garnett (1900‒1991), author and artist, lived here. She wrote “The Family from One End Street,” thought to be based in Lewes, which won the Carnegie Medal for best children’s book in 1938. Her painting “Lewes Gasworks from South Street” is in the Barb

Thomas Matthew, a Presbyterian woollen draper in the High Street, bequeathed his house on this site for the benefit of the poor of the parish of St. Michael-in-Lewes in 1688. The almshouses were closed in 1960.

Built around 1430 as part of a larger building encompassing 1 to 5 Keere Street and 95 to 96 High Street. 1 Keere Street became a separate house in 1539. Over the centuries it has housed a butcher, a bucket maker and, from 1780 until 1946, a bakery.
Pipe Passage. Named after 19th century clay pipe kiln. Follows Saxon and medieval access to town wall defences.

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Mapped outline, terrain and present-day surroundings from open data. No historic reconstruction.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
